Facts, in short, as stated in the writ petition as regards claim of the land, are that, the land measuring 0.60 acre in RS plot No. 5210 of Khatian No. 24019 of Mouza Madhayam Halishahar, PS Double Mooring, Chittagong was acquired by the government for development of the Chittagong Port by the Gazette notification No. 13543 dated 11th November, 1954 and that possession was made over to the requiring body Port Railway authority, that after bifurcation of Port and Railway the land in question was made over to the Port Trust on 1-7-1960 and since then the Port Authority was in possession of the land, that on 6-12-1989 the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 trespassed on the land in question and raised unauthorised kutcha structures, that in spite of the protest of the port authority to the' erection of the said unauthorised structures by the respondents and asking them to remove the structures they did not pay any heed to that and that also did not remove the unauthorised structures, that thereafter the Port Authority served notice for removal of the structures but the' respondent Nos. 1 and 2 did not remove the structures, that then the Port Authority filed an application under section 3(3) of the Ordinance before the Authorised Officer appointed under the provisions of the said Ordinance for eviction of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, that respondent Nos. I and 2 appeared, before the Authorised Officer and submitted written statement claiming them not trespassers or unauthorised occupants of the land in question and that claimed that they are the owners of the land on the basis of oral transfer between Krishna, Chandra Dutta, a rayat under the Zamindar Nazir Ahmed and others and that a suit filed by them seeking declaration of title, is pending relating to the land in question before the 3rd Court of Assistant Judge, Chittagong. 

 3. Authorised Officer upon perusal of the Gazette notification dated 11-11-1954, BS survey records recording the land in the name of the Port Authority and the contents of the 3rd schedule of part IV at page 98 of the Port Act, BP Khatian No.4, etc. and that also upon hearing the respondents who in spite of their repeated taking time for producing papers in support of their claim in respect of the land ultimately did not produce any paper in support of their claim in the land in question and that upon the finding that since acquisition in the year 1954 the Railway Authority being the owner of the land held that the Port Authority is the real owner of the property in question and that the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are trespassers as they have no legal basis for claiming the land in question and that they illegalty and unauthorisedly are possessing the land and thereupon made order for eviction 9f them from the land in question.
